item.title: Rupee jumps 1% after RBI redirects oil dollar demand, raises cost of some FX hedges
item.description: The Indian rupee surged about 1% on Monday after the central bank moved to curb spot and forward dollar demand through fresh policy measures, easing pressure on a currency that has lost 6.5% so far this year.
item.dc:creator: Nimesh Vora, Jaspreet Kalra
item.content:encoded: The Indian rupee surged about 1% on Monday after the central bank moved to curb spot and forward dollar demand through fresh policy measures, easing pressure on a currency that has lost 6.5% so far this year. The rupee rose 1% to 95.74 per dollar, up from Friday's close of 96.73 and outperforming largely rangebound Asian peers. Citi economists said recent central bank measures could trigger a knee-jerk appreciation before the rupee consolidates. "The package raises the near-term cost of rupee depreciation trades; it does not remove the underlying balance of payments pressures," they said in a Monday note. The Reserve Bank of India on Saturday [USN:L1N45W00Y TEXT:"unveiled a series of measures"] aimed at addressing two key sources of pressure on the rupee: persistent dollar demand from oil marketing companies, which has been amplified by high crude prices, and demand from corporates seeking to hedge against further currency weakness. Expectations of longer-term weakness pushed importers to step up purchases of forward dollars to [USN:L1N45R06L TEXT:"record"] levels last month. That hedging demand, in turn, added strain on the currency, creating a cycle of depreciation expectations, increased hedging and further weakness in the rupee. On Monday, the RBI also likely [USN:L4N45Y08R TEXT:"intervened"] in the FX market to bolster the rupee's gains via dollar sales by state-run banks, traders said. THE RBI STEPS IN The central bank barred firms from re-booking cancelled rupee-linked derivatives, cut the threshold for transactions without underlying exposure and required banks to set aside 20% cash against certain FX contracts, potentially raising hedging costs. The cash requirement applies only to hedging of current account transactions, such as import of goods or services, and excludes capital-account-related transactions like foreign portfolio investors hedging Indian investments. The reserve requirements could [USN:L1N45W02J TEXT:"increase hedging costs"] for importers by 80-150 basis points, depending on how much of the additional cost lenders pass on to clients, bankers said. RALLY FACES A TEST While the rupee has rallied sharply in the aftermath of the RBI's measures, the sustainability of the recovery will depend on whether underlying pressures subside, analysts say. "Unless BoP pressures ease more broadly, gradual INR depreciation is likely to resume once their initial impact fades," analysts at ANZ said. The firm has retained its medium-term INR depreciation view and said it will reassess levels after reviewing hedging and FX reserve data in the coming weeks. India's FX reserves [USN:AZN4TO3PS TEXT:"declined"] to $734 billion as of October 2 after hitting a record high of $785 billion in September. The FX pile had been bolstered by over $140 billion in inflows garnered under policy measures to draw capital from overseas Indians and via offshore borrowings by banks and state-run firms.

item.title: IMF says AI investment keeps global growth around 3%, with major Asia benefits
item.description: Strong investment in AI infrastructure is keeping global growth at around 3%, yielding major benefits for many Asian economies that supply the hardware, such as Thailand, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal, Rae Wee
item.content:encoded: Strong investment in AI infrastructure is keeping global growth at around 3%, yielding major benefits for many Asian economies that supply the hardware, such as Thailand, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said on Monday. The artificial intelligence investment boom was already delivering a "demand shock, an investment shock" that could boost growth in advanced Asian economies by a half to one full percentage point, and emerging Asian economies by 0.2 to 0.8 percentage point, she said. "AI, love it, hate it. It's already here," Georgieva said. "That shift into higher gear is what is keeping the world economy growing at around 3%, despite the fact we are being dragged down by the energy supply shock," she told hundreds of participants on the first day of a [USN:L1N45U032 TEXT:"weeklong set of meetings"] of the IMF and World Bank in the Thai capital. The IMF in July forecast global growth at 3% in 2026. It will release an updated outlook on Tuesday. Some 18,000 people are expected to attend the meetings this week, including finance officials from the IMF's 191 members. Several ministers will skip the meeting to focus on domestic priorities, including US Treasury Secretary Scott [USN:L1N45V0KM TEXT:"Bessent"] and Spanish Finance Minister Arcadi España, sources familiar with the matter said. AI WILL HAVE PROFOUND CONSEQUENCES Georgieva said AI amounted to a "slow-moving tsunami" that would have profound consequences for jobs, growth, education and even how governments generate revenue through taxation, given the expected shift from labor to capital. The IMF estimates that AI could lead to 40% of jobs being augmented, downgraded or eliminated, over time, she said. An initial study showed that 10% of jobs in the US already required AI skills. While routine, repetitive jobs were shrinking, low-paying jobs were increasing in two lower-paying sectors, construction and data centers. "It is a transformative technology. It so completely changes how we work, how we live," she said, noting that an AI assistant now gave her a 30-second message about her schedule each day. The US, China and India are the most important producers in the AI supply chain, but many of the firms building the needed infrastructure are in Asia, Georgieva said, referencing Thailand, host of this year's annual meetings. AI IMPACT ON ENTRY-LEVEL JOBS World Bank President Ajay Banga, who has made jobs a central focus of his presidency, said the development bank was focused on leveraging "small AI", which is not dependent on large language models, to generate enormous productivity gains for farmers, healthcare systems, educators and others in emerging markets. Singapore's President Tharman Shanmugaratnam, speaking at the same event, said governments should address how AI was reducing job opportunities for graduates. "There is a particular problem that we have to address very soon ... and that is that, the first rung in employment, your first job upon graduation, is now seeing less demand," he said. He said the world should also guard against AI resulting in a "new divergence" in growth and job creation between developing and advanced economies. "AI is going to widen the divergence if we are too passive about it," he said. "So we've got to do everything we can to first use AI to create good jobs and to create jobs that can be done well by human beings, can allow them to ride up a career ladder despite AI."

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝優勝決定Ｓ第1戦、ドジャースが逆転負け 大谷は1安打
item.description: ［１１日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１１日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）は１１日、ナ・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ（７回戦制）第１戦を行い、大谷翔平選手が先発出場したドジャースはブルワーズに１─２で敗れ、先勝を許した。

ドジャースは、二回に四球で出塁した大谷がテオスカー・ヘルナンデス外野手の右前打で進塁後、アンディ・パヘス外野手の適時打でホームを踏んで先制。しかし、先発のタリク・スクバル投手が四回にブライス・チュラング内野手のソロ本塁打を浴びて同点とされると、五回に逆転を許した。

「４番・指名打者」で出場した大谷は３打数１安打、１得点、１四球、１三振の内容だった。

item.title: トランプ氏のテレビ広告差し止め、米地裁 税金使用巡り
item.description:
Luc Cohen
[１１日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Luc Cohen

[１１日 ロイター] - 米ニューヨークの連邦地裁は１１日、トランプ政権による税金を使った政治広告を一時差し止める判断を下した。トランプ大統領を称賛する公費負担のテレビ広告が９月下旬から放映され始め、超党派の反発を招いていた。

監視団体コモン・コーズなどの原告は、こうした広告は政府広報ではなく、１１月３日の中間選挙で共和党候補を支援するための政治的な宣伝だとして提訴していた。

１０日に裁判所へ別途提出された文書によると、トランプ政権は地裁の差し止め命令に先立ち、広告の放映を取りやめる計画を既に立てていた。

トランプ氏は５日、広告は「偉大な米国を前向きに宣伝するもの」と考えているが、今後は税金で費用を賄わないと表明した。ホワイトハウスも今週、今後は同氏の政治活動委員会（ＰＡＣ）「ＭＡＧＡ」が広告費を負担すると発表した。

ホワイトハウスは、既に放映された広告についてトランプ氏のＰＡＣが税金を返還することはないとしている。これらの広告の最後には、米政府が費用を負担したと明記されている。司法省は地裁の命令に関するコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。

民主党全国委員会（ＤＮＣ）もワシントンの連邦裁判所に別途提訴し、広告の是非を争っている。

item.title: 英首相、16年ＥＵ離脱国民投票に「ロシアが干渉」 仏独に警告
item.description:
Andrew MacAskill
[ロンドン １１日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Andrew MacAskill

[ロンドン １１日 ロイター] - 英国のバーナム首相は、２０１６年の欧州連合（ＥＵ）離脱（ブレグジット）の是非を問う国民投票にロシアが干渉したと述べ、フランスとドイツの有権者に対し、ロシアが支援する政治への影響工作に警戒するよう呼びかけた。

１０年前の国民投票にロシアが干渉した証拠があると公言した英首相は同氏が初めて。

バーナム氏は１１日に公開されたポッドキャストのインタビューで「首相官邸入りに際し、１６年の国民投票にロシアの干渉があったのかと尋ねた。あったという明確な回答を得た」と語った。

ロシアがどのように干渉したと考えているかについては説明せず、発言の根拠となった証拠の詳細も明らかにしなかった。

在ロンドンのロシア大使館はコメント要請に返答していない。

ロシアはこれまで、ＥＵ離脱を巡る国民投票への干渉を否定し、英国が反ロシアのヒステリーに陥っていると主張してきた。

バーナム氏は、欧州の民主主義国家の有権者は政治を混乱させようとする動きについて、より十分な情報を得る必要があると指摘。「こうしたことを今、明確に記録に残すのが重要だ。こうした政治の動きの一部が、われわれの敵、つまりロシアによって引き起こされているとドイツやフランスの有権者が理解する助けになると考えている」と語った。

英議会の情報安全保障委員会が２０年に公表した報告書によると、英政府は１６年の国民投票にロシアが干渉したかどうかを解明できなかった。

item.title: China Sanctions Paraguay, Belize Ministers Over Taiwan Ties
item.description: China placed sanctions from Monday on Paraguay’s communications minister as well as the foreign minister of Belize, over their countries’ ties with Taiwan which Beijing claims as its own territory. Paraguay and Belize are two of just 12 countries to maintain formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan. China says Taiwan is one …
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
China placed sanctions from Monday on Paraguay’s communications minister as well as the foreign minister of Belize, over their countries’ ties with Taiwan which Beijing claims as its own territory.

Paraguay and Belize are two of just 12 countries to maintain formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan. China says Taiwan is one of its provinces with no right to the trappings of a state, a view Taipei’s government strongly rejects.

The sanctions are largely symbolic given ministers from Taiwan’s diplomatic allies generally never travel to China. Such sanctions have previously mainly been applied to Western politicians for their support of democratically governed Taiwan.

Neither Paraguay’s Ministry of Information and Communication Technologies nor Belize’s foreign ministry immediately responded to requests for comment outside of regular office hours. Taiwan’s foreign ministry had no immediate comment.

China’s foreign ministry cited national sovereignty and security as reasons for the measures, saying some Belize and Paraguay politicians have been “anti-China” in pushing for their nations to maintain diplomatic ties with Taiwan.

The measures include barring entry visas to Hong Kong and Macau, and prohibition on Chinese organisations and individuals from engaging in transactions, cooperation or other activities, the ministry said in two notices.

Belize Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca met his Taiwan counterpart, Lin Chia-lung, in Belize last month. In June, Paraguay Minister of Information and Communication Technologies Gustavo Villate met Taiwan Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi in Paraguay.

China has stepped up pressure on Taiwan’s remaining diplomatic allies to sever ties with Taipei.

The last country to do so was the tiny Pacific Islands nation of Nauru, in 2024, while the previous year Honduras ended its decades-long ties with Taiwan.

item.title: Gold retreats as markets await key US inflation data
item.description: Gold eased from a more than one-week high on Monday as investors stayed cautious ahead of key US inflation data due this week for fresh clues on the Federal Reserve's interest rate path.
item.dc:creator: Sukanya Mitra
item.content:encoded: Gold eased from a more than one-week high on Monday as investors stayed cautious ahead of key US inflation data due this week for fresh clues on the Federal Reserve's interest rate path. Spot gold fell 0.2% to $4,185.13 per ounce by 0714 GMT, after hitting its highest since October 2 earlier in the day. US gold futures for December delivery dropped 0.2% to $4,209.70. "In the short term, a cooler-than-expected US inflation reading would be the clearest near-term catalyst, as it would reduce the odds of further Fed tightening and ease pressure on real yield," said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade. "Longer term, sustained central bank buying and any further de-escalation in geopolitical flashpoints that brings oil and the dollar lower would improve the backdrop for gold." US President Donald Trump [USN:L1N45X021 TEXT:"made a surprise announcement"] of an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine on Sunday that he said was "effective immediately", but Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he was still waiting to see details of the deal. Oil prices fell on [USN:L1N45X085 TEXT:"expectations"] of more Russian supplies. The US dollar [USN:L1N45Y01U TEXT:"held its ground"] near its strongest level in a year and a half reached last week, making greenback-priced bullion more expensive for buyers holding other currencies. While gold is typically seen as a hedge against inflation, higher interest rates tend to diminish the non-yielding metal's appeal. Markets are now awaiting the US Consumer Price Index (CPI) report on Wednesday, followed by the Producer Price Index (PPI) and retail sales data on Thursday. Traders see a 19% chance of a rate hike in October and an 84% probability of an increase by December, according to CME’s FedWatch tool. Meanwhile, [USN:L1N45V0J1 TEXT:"US consumer sentiment"] slumped further in early October as the rising cost of living because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy. Among other metals, spot silver rose 0.2% to $60.95 per ounce, platinum gained 0.8% to $1,701.18 and palladium climbed 1% to $1,159.62.

item.title: Rugby league-Kiwi Hughes wants to make amends for 2022 World Cup heartbreak
item.description: MELBOURNE, Oct 12 : Four years after New Zealand's heartbreaking Rugby League World Cup semi-final defeat by Australia, halfback Jahrome Hughes is still haunted by a missed opportunity to send the Kiwis into the final.Hughes scored a try and was among New Zealand's best players in the 16-14 loss in 2022, but

MELBOURNE, Oct 12 : Four years after New Zealand's heartbreaking Rugby League World Cup semi-final defeat by Australia, halfback Jahrome Hughes is still haunted by a missed opportunity to send the Kiwis into the final. Hughes scored a try and was among New Zealand's best players in the 16-14 loss in 2022, but a speculative grubber kick late in the match squandered a promising attacking opportunity as the Kiwis chased victory. Hughes has carried the regret ever since and is determined to make amends at this year's World Cup, starting with New Zealand's opener against defending champions Australia in Sydney on Thursday. "Getting so close in 2022 in the World Cup and losing to Australia in the semi-final, I still hold a bit of fire in my belly from that," Hughes told reporters on Monday.

"I take a lot of blame for losing that game." Hughes has since established himself among the game's elite playmakers, winning the 2024 Dally M Medal as the National Rugby League's best player with Melbourne Storm and helping New Zealand thrash Australia 30-0 in the 2023 Pacific Championships final on home soil in Hamilton. But the 32-year-old has not played for his country since 2023, with neck and shoulder injuries wiping out his international prospects. He said his return to the national squad had rekindled the excitement he felt as a youngster dreaming of representing the Kiwis. "I've had a couple of years away from them. It just makes you realise you can't take this jersey for granted," he said. "I'm one of the older guys now, but I felt like a little kid coming back into camp yesterday and seeing everyone." New Zealand have not won the World Cup since their breakthrough triumph in 2008, with Australia claiming the last three titles. Hughes hopes a second World Cup title for the Kiwis could boost the game back home, where rugby union and the All Blacks still dominate. "Just thinking back to 2008 when I was a kid and seeing how that win made me feel, if we were able to lift that trophy at the end of this World Cup, the things it would do for the kids back home in New Zealand and all the supporters back home, it would be truly special," he said. In a scheduling quirk, the All Blacks will meet Australia in a rugby union test at Stadium Australia on Saturday, two days after the Kiwis-Kangaroos clash in the same city. Flyhalf Beauden Barrett said he and his All Blacks teammates would cheer on the Kiwis at Sydney Football Stadium before they knuckle down for the second Bledisloe Cup test against the Wallabies. "We've got a bit of free time, so it'll be a great spectacle," Barrett told reporters on Monday. "It's just down the road, too. So, yeah, the town's buzzing."

Source: Reuters

item.title: China sanctions 'pawn' Paraguay, Belize ministers over Taiwan ties
item.description: China on Monday placed sanctions on Paraguay's communications minister and the foreign minister of Belize over their countries' ties with Taiwan, saying they were "pawns" who have smeared and attacked Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Liz Lee
item.content:encoded: China on Monday placed sanctions on Paraguay's communications minister and the foreign minister of Belize over their countries' ties with Taiwan, saying they were "pawns" who have smeared and attacked Beijing. Paraguay and Belize are two of just 12 countries to maintain formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan. China says Taiwan is one of its provinces with no right to the trappings of a state, a view Taipei's government strongly rejects. The sanctions are largely symbolic given ministers from Taiwan's diplomatic allies generally don't travel to China. Such sanctions have previously mainly been applied to Western politicians for their support of democratically governed Taiwan. Neither Paraguay's Ministry of Information and Communication Technologies nor Belize's foreign ministry immediately responded to requests for comment outside of regular office hours. Taiwan's foreign ministry had no immediate comment. China's foreign ministry cited national sovereignty and security as reasons for the measures, saying some Belize and Paraguay politicians have been "anti-China" in pushing for their nations to maintain diplomatic ties with Taiwan. The measures include barring entry visas to Hong Kong and Macau, and prohibition on Chinese organisations and individuals from engaging in transactions, cooperation or other activities, the ministry said in two notices. Belize Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca met his Taiwan counterpart, Lin Chia-lung, in Belize last month. In June, Paraguay Minister of Information and Communication Technologies Gustavo Villate met Taiwan Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi in Paraguay. 'PAWNS' Speaking in Beijing, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said the politicians were "willing to serve as pawns" for Taiwan. "They have seriously interfered in China's internal affairs, spread false information about Chinese cyberattacks and attacked and smeared China, causing a bad international impact," she added, without elaborating. The remaining countries with ties to Taiwan should not be "repeatedly manipulated by Taiwan independence separatist forces," she added. "Doing so has no future, (it) will only cause them to miss development opportunities." Shortly before the Chinese announcement, the Belize embassy in Taiwan posted on its Facebook page a message celebrating the October 11 anniversary of the 37th year since the two established ties. "Together, we look forward to a future of growth, opportunity, and lasting friendship," the embassy wrote. China has stepped up pressure on Taiwan's remaining diplomatic allies to sever ties with Taipei. The last country to do so was the tiny Pacific Islands nation of Nauru, in 2024, while the previous year Honduras ended its decades-long ties with Taiwan.

item.title: 台湾、中国による一連の実弾演習を注視 沿岸各地で今週実施
item.description: [台北 １２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[台北 １２日 ロイター] - 台湾の顧立雄国防部長（国防相）は１２日、中国が今週、沿岸各地で実施する一連の実弾演習について、台湾軍は注視していると述べた。

中国海事局は８日以降、南シナ海から北東部の遼寧省に至る５カ所の海域について航行禁止の通知を出した。ただ、台湾周辺の海域は含まれていない。

台湾に最も近いのは中国東部・浙江省の沖合。通知によると、演習は今週いっぱい続く予定だ。

顧氏は立法院（国会）で記者団に対し、初期評価では沿岸砲兵部隊と関連部隊による射撃訓練とみられると説明。

「ただ、われわれは『敵の動きを可能な限り幅広く想定する』という原則に従っており、射撃であれ軍事訓練であれ、引き続き活動を注意深く監視する」と述べた。

台湾の頼清徳総統は１０日の双十節（建国記念日）の演説で、台湾は平和を大切にするが自由を放棄することはなく、台湾の人々が生存する権利は尊重されなければならないと述べた。

中国は今週の演習と頼氏の演説を関連付けてはいないが、中国国防省は１１日、頼氏が中国の脅威を誇張し、「武力によって独立を図ろうとしている」と批判した。

item.title: ネパール土石流で5人不明、住宅・橋など流される 避難呼びかけ
item.description:
Gopal Sharma
[カトマンズ １１日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Gopal Sharma

[カトマンズ １１日 ロイター] - ネパール中部で１１日、土石流が発生し、国家災害対策当局によると、５人が行方不明となっている。死傷者は報告されていない。軍は外国人１人を含む４９人が救助されたと発表した。

住宅やインフラが流され、当局は住民に安全な場所への避難を呼びかけた。

当局によると、カトマンズの西約１００キロに位置するゴルカ郡チュムヌブリ村で地滑りが発生し、川がせき止められたことで下流で土石流が起きた。

十数軒の住宅とつり橋２本が流されたほか、水力発電事業の作業拠点が被害を受け、建設機材の一部が流された。

泥流を伴う川の水位が上昇しており、ゴルカ郡と隣接するダディン郡を結ぶ幹線道路の橋も流されたという。

当局はゴルカ、タナフン、チトワン、東ナワルパラシ、西ナワルパラシの各郡の川沿いに暮らす住民に警戒を呼びかけた。

ネパールでは８月にも大規模な土石流があり、１４５７人が死亡、数千人が依然として行方不明となっている。

item.title: US Republicans, Democrats want Trump to reverse course on Russia diesel
item.description: Donald Trump's administration failed to consult with Congress or submit any explanation of its decision, something required by law, seven senators said.

US Republicans, Democrats want Trump to reverse course on Russia diesel

Donald Trump's administration failed to consult with Congress or submit any explanation of its decision, something required by law, seven senators said.

US Senator Thom Tillis at Capitol Hill in Washington, DC, on Aug 4, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Elizabeth Frantz)

Republican and Democratic US senators called on President Donald Trump on Sunday (Oct 11) to "reverse course" on his diesel supply deal with Russia, saying it runs counter to US law barring imports of energy until Russia ends its aggression against Ukraine. "Congress explicitly banned Russian energy imports in 2022 to prevent American dollars from financing (Russian President Vladimir) Putin’s brutal war against Ukraine," the seven senators - four of Trump's fellow Republicans and three Democrats - said in a statement. They also said that the administration failed to consult with Congress or submit any explanation of its decision, something also required by law. "The United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians. The Administration must immediately reverse course," the statement said.

It was only the latest bipartisan criticism of Trump's deal, a shift from his party's near-unanimous support for Trump's foreign policy decision weeks before Nov 3 midterm elections that will determine whether his Republicans will retain their control of Congress. It was issued by Republican Senators Susan Collins of Maine, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, Thom Tillis of North Carolina and John Curtis of Utah and Democrats Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut and Ron Wyden of Oregon. Tillis had said earlier on Sunday that the diesel deal may be illegal and would put American lives at risk.

Related:

Russia hits Ukraine power plants despite Trump energy ceasefire claim

Ukraine's Zelenskyy says he will organise elections if Russia agrees to 60-day ceasefire

Trump said on Friday that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets , and his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its war on Ukraine. “I do believe there’s a legitimate case for saying the president’s not following the law,” Tillis, who is retiring from the Senate in January, told NBC's "Meet the Press." Prices for diesel - used for agriculture, heating homes and trucking - are near record highs and could hurt Republicans in next month's congressional elections. Analysts have said that Trump's agreement with Moscow was unlikely to lead to sustained lower fuel prices. ADMINISTRATION DEFENDS PACT US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on Sunday that the Trump administration will follow through with the deal using existing legal authority, and the agreement was good for the American people and would bring prices down. "We're going to do it with all the legal authorities we have. So, you know, anyone in Congress who says whether it's an old bill or the current Lindsey Graham bill (that) prohibits us from doing it is wrong," Bessent told Fox & Friends. Trump last month signed a sweeping Russia sanctions bill into law, called the "Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026", to honour the South Carolina Republican and longtime Russia hawk who died in July. Some other Republicans had also criticised the diesel plan. Retiring Representative Don Bacon of Nebraska said on X on Friday that "propping up Putin's war economy is morally wrong as he uses that money to bomb cities". Mike Pence, Trump's former vice president, called his decision to lift sanctions on Russian oil a "betrayal" of Graham’s legacy and urged the president to "rescind" it.

Related:

Trump rules out diesel export ban after European release

Trump moves to cut diesel costs with order on tax-free fuel

As Trump's poll numbers have cratered, congressional Republicans have increasingly distanced themselves from the president, on matters ranging from the conflict in Iran to the trade war with Canada. But the Senate's No 2 Republican, John Barrasso of Wyoming, defended the diesel pact, telling CBS' Face the Nation that Trump is focused on bringing costs down. "The president is balancing and has to make tough decisions," Barrasso said. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in a call on Sunday with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy made it clear that the diesel deal "is in direct opposition to the efforts of Ukraine, Canada, and our allies to create peace and stability in Europe," his office said in a statement. In a social media post on Sunday, Trump claimed that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to what he described as an "energy ceasefire" taking effect immediately, but did not elaborate. Zelenskyy said he was still waiting to see details of that agreement. "Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it is important that Russia support it as well," Zelenskyy said on the Telegram app. There was no word from Moscow on the announcement, which followed days of US pressure on Ukraine to halt its attacks on Russian oil refineries.

Source: Reuters/ec

item.title: AirAsia in talks with Malaysian government over potential funding support, sources say
item.description: AirAsia co-founder Tony Fernandes met with officials from Malaysia's finance ministry two weeks ago to discuss potential government support for Southeast Asia's largest low-cost airline, said three people with knowledge of the matter.
item.dc:creator: Julie Zhu, Yantoultra Ngui, Anne Marie Roantree
item.content:encoded: AirAsia (AIRG.KL) co-founder Tony Fernandes met with officials from Malaysia's finance ministry two weeks ago to discuss potential government support for Southeast Asia's largest low-cost airline, said three people with knowledge of the matter. The talks reflect growing government concerns about the financial health of the country's largest domestic carrier following a spike in jet fuel prices, the people said. Discussions centred on the prospect of the government backing AirAsia's fundraising efforts provided the airline agreed to proposed conditions, which remain under discussion, two of the people said. Reuters could not immediately determine details of the proposed conditions. Fernandes, speaking for the airline as its co-founder and adviser, told Reuters in an exclusive interview on Friday that he had met with officials from Malaysia's finance and transport ministries during the week starting September 28 at his request. He said the discussions focused on aviation-related costs such as airport charges and fuel, not financial assistance. "Obviously, like every airline in the world, we are telling government that this is a tough period," he said. "There have been no discussions on financial assistance with the government," Fernandes added. "I meet with government officials all the time...just because I meet them doesn't mean we're talking about financial assistance." He said he had not approached the government for help, and the government had not raised concerns with him about AirAsia's funding or offered support. Fernandes said he was "100%" confident AirAsia could navigate the situation without state assistance, as it had during the pandemic. But Fernandes said AirAsia would not turn away help if offered from any government in the countries where it operates, including Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia. "We will never say no to it. We would be foolish to do so," he said. He added that he had previously asked the government to help the airline secure loans from Malaysian banks rather than borrowing overseas, and still sought such support as he preferred local-currency loans with better interest rates and terms. Representatives from Alton Aviation Consultancy, which Reuters previously reported the finance ministry has hired to [USN:L8N44U0IG TEXT:"assess loss-making AirAsia's funding needs"], also attended the meeting, two of the people with knowledge of the discussions said. Malaysia's finance ministry declined to comment. Alton did not respond to requests for comment. Malaysian Transport Minister Anthony Loke told a press conference on Monday that he had not had any meetings with AirAsia in the last two to three weeks, nor had other transport ministry officials. "They (AirAsia) may have had discussions with the Ministry of Finance. These airlines do have regular meetings with the government," Loke said. His comments were made after the publication of Reuters' report about the meeting between Fernandes and the finance ministry. AirAsia shares were trading 5% lower on Monday afternoon. The airline has been hit by soaring jet fuel costs that surged 66% in the second quarter from the prior quarter to an average of $183 a barrel, stemming from the US-Israeli war on Iran . The meeting followed a Reuters report last month that Malaysia's government had asked Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air whether they could [USN:L8N4520SK TEXT:"absorb AirAsia's domestic market share"] as part of scenario planning while authorities monitor the carrier's financial health. AirAsia's shares fell as much as 21% to near four-year lows the next day. The government has grown increasingly concerned about AirAsia's financial position because of the knock-on effects its weakness would have on air connectivity, tourism and related businesses such as state-linked airport operator Malaysia Airports Holdings Berhad, said two of the people. AirAsia controls about 60% of Malaysia's domestic aviation market and employs 26,000 people, according to Fernandes. The airline had cash and bank balances of 954 million ringgit ($233.65 million) and current liabilities of 18.4 billion ringgit as of June 30. TOWN HALL The meeting with government officials followed a company town hall Fernandes held on September 28 at AirAsia's headquarters, where he told staff that the airline would overcome its current difficulties, two of the people said. Fernandes said he had told employees it was a tough time for all airlines. "We've been through many tough times before. We will come out of it stronger," he recalled saying. "The big difference between this and COVID is we can actually fly." At a press conference on September 18, he said there had been [USN:L4N45A054 TEXT:"no discussions with the government"], the carrier had "strong liquidity" and "we do not need rescue, bailout, whatever." AirAsia [USN:L1N45A03J TEXT:"reported"] a net loss of 831 million ringgit ($204 million) for the second quarter ended June 30, hit by higher jet fuel costs and foreign-exchange losses of 331 million ringgit. The airline has said it is targeting up to $1 billion from international debt markets plus 700 million ringgit in local credit facilities, primarily to refinance existing debt. Its stock has lost more than 70% of its value this year. Fernandes said on Friday he expected the $1 billion fundraising to be completed between December and February, with half used to refinance expensive loans and the rest for working capital and paying off "extended liabilities." Fernandes said AirAsia was budgeting for 12 months of high oil prices and had yet to see demand weaken, with the percentage of seats filled above 80% even though jet fuel prices had risen as high as $200 a barrel. "Above $200, it hasn't been tested yet," he said. "At some point, it will create demand destruction. I'm not sure where that point is." ($1 = 4.0830 ringgit)

item.title: ジブチ沖で移民船転覆、子ども含む139人死亡＝国連機関
item.description: [ナイロビ １１日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ナイロビ １１日 ロイター] - 国連の国際移住機関（ＩＯＭ）は１１日、アフリカ東部ジブチ沖で、移民３０５人を乗せイエメンに向かっていた船が８日夜から９日未明の間に転覆し、少なくとも子ども１５人を含む１３９人が死亡したと発表した。約８４人が行方不明になっているという。

声明によると、この事故で約８２人が生き残った。

ＩＯＭが公開した写真には、履き古されたサンダルやスニーカーが海岸に打ち上げられている様子が写っていた。

ＩＯＭジブチ事務所の代表は「われわれのチームは現地当局と共に現場で緊急支援を行っている」と説明。「この悲劇は、経済的な機会を求めてこの移住ルートを通る移民が直面する危険を改めて浮き彫りにしている」と語った。

ＩＯＭは声明で「イエメンで暴力が続いているにもかかわらず、移民は湾岸諸国への到達を望み、今なお危険な旅に出ている」と指摘した。

ＩＯＭの当局者はロイターに対し、ジブチを経由する「東部ルート」で、数年にわたり多数の移民の移動を記録してきたと述べた。

いわゆる東部ルートには、海難事故のほか、上陸後の人身売買や恣意的な逮捕など、多くの危険が伴う。ＩＯＭの「行方不明移民プロジェクト」によると、２０２５年にはこのルートを使う人が１８％増加する中、９００人超の移民が死亡または行方不明となった。

item.title: Taiwan says it is closely monitoring a series of Chinese live-fire drills
item.description: Taiwan defence minister Wellington Koo said on Monday that the military is monitoring a series of Chinese live-fire drills taking place along the country's coast this week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Taiwan defence minister Wellington Koo said on Monday that the military is monitoring a series of Chinese live-fire drills taking place along the country's coast this week. Starting from Thursday, the China Maritime Safety Administration announced no-sail notices for five areas, from the South China Sea up to the northeastern province of Liaoning, though none around Taiwan itself. The closest one to Taiwan is off China's eastern province of Zhejiang. The drills are scheduled to last all week, according to the notices. Speaking to reporters in parliament, Koo said the preliminary assessment is that these activities were firing drills by coastal artillery and related units. "However, we adhere to the principle of 'anticipating the enemy as broadly as possible', so we will continue to closely monitor their activities, whether firing or military training," he said. President Lai Ching-te, in his [USN:L1N45W00U TEXT:"National Day speech"] on Saturday, said Taiwan cherishes peace but will not give up its freedom, and there must be respect for the right of Taiwan's people to exist. China, which views Taiwan as its own territory, condemned his remarks, as it always does. China views Lai as a "separatist" and has rebuffed his repeated offers of talks. While China has not linked the drills this week to Lai's speech, on Sunday the country's defence ministry said he was exaggerating the threat from China and trying to "seek independence through force". "The People's Liberation Army's regular training and exercises around Taiwan are meant to deter reckless 'Taiwan independence' moves and outside interference, and to safeguard the security and well-being of the Taiwanese people. This is entirely justified," it said. PAST WAR GAMES China's military operates around Taiwan on an almost daily basis, though it has not held full war games since late December, which were in response to an $11 billion arms sale announced by Washington, the largest ever. Last week, the US State Department said China's maritime actions off Taiwan's east coast are "deeply destabilising" and only worsen tension, after Reuters reported the first known sighting of a Chinese [USN:L4N45S05G TEXT:"militia boat"] in those waters in August. Speaking in Beijing on Monday, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said those waters belonged to China and its activities there were "beyond reproach". "It has never been China that stirs up trouble and undermines stability in this sea," she told reporters, without elaborating. Lai says only Taiwan's people can decide their future, and that Beijing has no right to claim the island as its territory.

A US judge on Sunday (Oct 11) blocked the Trump administration from using taxpayer money to pay for political advertisements, after publicly funded television ads glorifying US President Donald Trump began airing in late September and sparked a bipartisan backlash. Manhattan-based US District Judge Jennifer Rochon temporarily barred the advertisements after plaintiffs including watchdog group Common Cause brought a lawsuit alleging the ads were political propaganda designed to help Republican candidates in the Nov 3 midterm elections, not public service announcements. The Trump administration was already planning to stop running the ads before Rochon's order, according to a separate statement filed with the court on Saturday. The decision caps days of controversy over the taxpayer-funded advertisements, which were aired in the final weeks before the midterm elections.

“We won’t stop until this administration is held fully accountable, and no president from any party can waste and abuse taxpayer funds for propaganda ever again," said Common Cause President and CEO Virginia Kase Solomón. Trump on Monday said he considered the ads to be a "positive promotion for our great USA" but that they would no longer be funded by taxpayers , and the White House said this week that the president's political action committee, MAGA PAC, would fund the ads going forward. The White House said Trump's political action committee will not reimburse taxpayers for the ads that have already run. The ads end with a disclaimer saying they were paid for by the US government. The Justice Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the judge's order. The plaintiffs, which also included a public employee union and a candidate for Alabama state representative, had asked Rochon to temporarily block the ads by Friday so that they could not air during weekend programming such as football games and Saturday Night Live. Democratic Party officials also challenged the ads in a separate suit brought in federal court in Washington.

item.title: ＮＢＡ＝ウォリアーズ、ポジェムスキーと5年契約延長へ 総額約174億円─報道
item.description: ［１１日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１１日　ロイター］ - 米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）のウォリアーズが、ガードのブランディン・ポジェムスキー（２３）と５年総額１億１０００万ドル（約１７４億円）の契約延長で合意したことが分かった。米スポーツ専門局ＥＳＰＮが１０日、代理人の話として報じた。

契約は全額保証され、最終年の２０３１─３２シーズンには相互オプションが付く。２６─２７シーズンに新人契約最終年の年俸５６０万ドルを受け取り、翌シーズンの年俸は１８９０万ドルとなる。

昨季は全８２試合（先発４３試合）に出場し、１試合平均１３．８得点、５．１リバウンド、３．７アシストを記録。３点シュート成功率は３７．１％で、成功数１５３本はステフィン・カリーの１９０本に次ぐチーム２位だった。

２３年のドラフト１巡目（全体１９位）で指名され、ＮＢＡ通算２２０試合（先発１０４試合）で平均１１．６得点、５．３リバウンド、３．６アシストを記録している。

ウォリアーズは２１日、敵地でレーカーズとのレギュラーシーズン開幕戦に臨む。

item.title: 陸上＝シカゴマラソン、赤崎が9位 大迫は14位 キプルト優勝
item.description: ［１１日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１１日　ロイター］ - シカゴ・マラソンは１１日、米シカゴ市街地のコースで行われ、男子は２０２４年パリ五輪６位の赤崎暁が２時間５分４７秒でフィニッシュし、日本人トップとなる９位に入った。日本記録を持つ大迫傑は１４位だった。

初マラソンの太田智樹は２６位。昨年２位のアモス・キプルト（ケニア）が２時間１分９秒で制した。

女子では赤崎優花が２時間２３分１８秒で１１位。ハウィ・フェイサ（エチオピア）がシャロン・ロケディ（ケニア）との激闘を制し、２時間１３分３３秒で２連覇を達成した。

item.title: Peak XV, Accel-backed Zetwerk seeks $2.64 billion valuation in India IPO
item.description: Peak XV Partners and Accel India-backed Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses is seeking a valuation of 255.83 billion rupees ($2.64 billion) in its initial public offering in India, a company filing showed on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Praveen Paramasivam, Vivek M
item.content:encoded: Peak XV Partners and Accel India-backed Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses is seeking a valuation of 255.83 billion rupees ($2.64 billion) in its initial public offering in India, a company filing showed on Monday. The $518 million IPO will open for public subscription from October 15 to 19, with the manufacturing platform's shares expected to begin trading on October 23. Anchor investors can submit bids on October 14. Zetwerk, which manufactures industrial and consumer products, counts wind turbine maker Siemens Gamesa, computer hardware company Acer India, the Indian Air Force and NTPC Renewable Energy among its customers. Amrit Acharya, co-founder and CEO of Zetwerk, told Reuters the business is "sufficiently diversified", at a time when geopolitical challenges, supply chain risks, and AI-driven opportunities and disruptions are forcing companies to rethink strategies. Energy products account for nearly 60% of the company's revenue, while precision products, which cater to industries including consumer electronics, EVs and wearables, contribute around 23% to the topline. The IPO comes during a busy period for India’s primary market, with billionaire Mukesh Ambani-backed Jio Platforms expected to launch what could be the country’s largest-ever IPO on October 21. More than 230 companies have raised $12.65 billion in India this year as of October 7, 8.3% more than a year earlier, LSEG data showed. Zetwerk's IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth up to 28.3 billion rupees and an offer for sale of 144.53 million shares by top shareholders and existing investors. The company set the price band at 143 to 151 rupees per share. Co-founders Amrit Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan, along with Creovate Innovation, are together selling 51.4 million shares, while early investors Peak XV Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Accel India are among other shareholders selling their stakes. The combined stake held by the company's founders and other major shareholders could fall to around 16% after the IPO from the current 20.66%, Acharya said. Zetwerk reported revenue from operations of 41.18 billion rupees for the April-June quarter, while its restated loss from continuing operations stood at 641.29 million rupees. Revenue rose more than 55% from a year earlier, while the loss narrowed from 8.81 billion rupees. The company plans to use IPO proceeds to prepay and repay borrowings as well as fund inorganic growth opportunities. ($1 = 96.7600 Indian rupees)

item.title: NFL injury roundup: Defensive injuries dot NFC North
item.description: Green Bay defensive tackle Javon Hargrave is likely done for the season with an Achilles tendon injury, Packers coach Matt LaFleur indicated after Sunday's 31-7 victory over the Chicago Bears.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Green Bay defensive tackle Javon Hargrave is likely done for the season with an Achilles tendon injury, Packers coach Matt LaFleur indicated after Sunday's 31-7 victory over the Chicago Bears. "Early indications look like Achilles," said LaFleur, who also said the injury "doesn't look good." Hargrave was injured chasing Bears quarterback Case Keenum in the fourth quarter. He fell without contact and was carted off the field with 1:53 remaining. Hargrave had one tackle and one quarterback hit before exiting. He has six stops in four games this season. It marks the second time in as many weeks that Green Bay lost a standout defender to an Achilles injury. Last week, linebacker Edgerrin Cooper was carted off and eventually determined to have an Achilles tear that will keep him out the rest of the year. --In the same game, the Bears lost linebacker T.J. Edwards and cornerback Tyrique Stevenson to hamstring injuries. Edwards had four tackles, including one tackle for loss, before his exit while Stevenson recorded two tackles and a pass deflection. Edwards is in his fourth season as a starting linebacker for Chicago and his eighth NFL campaign overall, while Stevenson is playing his fourth season since the Bears selected him in the second round of the 2023 draft. Coach Ben Johnson said after the game that quarterback Caleb Williams is "close" to returning from his Grade 2 hamstring strain suffered in Week 2. Tyson Bagent has started two of the past three games in Williams' place. --Elsewhere in the NFC North, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell said after his team's 45-21 road win against the Arizona Cardinals that linebacker Devin White will likely need surgery to repair a broken forearm. White suffered the injury in the first half and was taken from the sideline on a cart. It marked just his third game for the Lions after playing for the Raiders in 2025 and the Texans in 2024. He missed Weeks 3 and 4 as a healthy scratch. --San Francisco 49ers receiver Deebo Samuel suffered an apparent left hamstring injury with five minutes left in the third quarter and was ruled out for the remainder of the Niners' 32-29 win over the Seattle Seahawks. Samuel was hurt after a 2-yard rush on an end-around play on which he fumbled, giving Seattle the ball at San Francisco's 36-yard line. Samuel had two catches for 21 yards and two rushes for 4 yards before his exit. He had 14 receptions for 185 yards and three touchdowns entering the day. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan did not have an update on Samuel's condition postgame. --Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson suffered a concussion on the opening possession and missed the rest of Minnesota's 23-13 win against the host New Orleans Saints. Hockenson led Minnesota with 22 receptions through four games after catching 13 passes in a 15-10 victory against Miami last week. He caught a 7-yard pass from Kyler Murray on the second play on Sunday and was injured while being tackled by Pete Werner. He went to the locker room for evaluation and was ruled out shortly thereafter. --Cleveland Browns rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion sustained a head injury midway through the first quarter of his team's 17-12 loss to the New York Jets. Concepcion was injured in the first quarter when Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick crashed into him with a helmet-to-helmet hit. Concepcion remained down on the turf for a few minutes before being helped off the field. Fitzpatrick was penalized for the hit but Browns coach Todd Monken said it wasn't a dirty play on the part of the nine-year veteran. Concepcion had one catch for 5 yards before exiting. The first-round pick (24th overall) out of Texas A&M has 18 receptions for 149 yards through five games. Jets rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq also suffered a concussion Sunday. --New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) and starting left tackle Will Campbell (knee) were both injured during the first half of their 45-17 win against the Las Vegas Raiders. Henderson gained 22 yards on four carries and had one catch for 16 yards before he left the game. His injury will likely result in more playing time for Rhamondre Stevenson, who finished the game with 13 attempts for 64 yards and a touchdown. NFL Network reported that Campbell is believed to have suffered a knee sprain, with an MRI scheduled for Monday to confirm the severity of his injury. --The Houston Texans earned their first win of the season 26-3 over the winless Tennessee Titans but lost running back David Montgomery and safety Jalen Pitre along the way. Montgomery had five carries for 11 yards before exiting with a groin injury. Pitre injured his shoulder, and head coach DeMeco Ryans said both players were still being evaluated. --New York Giants right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor left his team's 27-27 tie against the Washington Commanders with a calf injury. Eluemunor told reporters postgame that he believes he strained the calf and did not expect it to be a long-term injury. --In London, the Philadelphia Eagles' backfield took another hit when Will Shipley picked up a foot injury in his first start of the season against Jacksonville. Shipley was the starting running back as Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby deal with hamstring and abdomen injuries, respectively. Shipley scored his first NFL touchdown in the first quarter before leaving with the injury before the period's end. The banged-up Eagles, who eventually lost 19-17 to the Jaguars, also had guard Tyler Steen (shoulder), edge rusher Jalyx Hunt (ankle, knee) and defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen) leave the game. The Jaguars lost long snapper Ross Matiscik to a shoulder injury and had to use DaVon Hamilton as a replacement, which led to some high snaps before Jacksonville pulled off a game-winning 57-yard field goal by Cam Little. The Jags also lost left tackle Anton Harrison (knee) and cornerback Montaric Brown (hamstring) during the game. --Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. sustained a rib injury on the final series of regulation against Baltimore. He missed one play and was replaced by Tua Tagovailoa, re-entered for another but didn't play in overtime as the visiting Ravens won 30-23. Penix said afterward that he doesn't believe it's a long-term injury. The team said he will undergo imaging on Monday. Cornerback C.J. Henderson (groin) did not return after being listed as questionable to start the third quarter. He recorded two tackles. --Ravens defensive lineman Broderick Washington (ankle) did not return after his injury in the fourth quarter against the Falcons. He recorded one tackle. --Field Level Media

item.title: パキスタン、カーン氏政党率いる州政府の機能停止 非常事態を宣言
item.description:
Asif Shahzad Ariba Shahid
[イスラマバード １１日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Asif Shahzad　Ariba Shahid

[イスラマバード １１日 ロイター] - パキスタンのザルダリ大統領は１１日、北西部カイバル・パクトゥンクワ州に非常事態を宣言し、州政府の機能を停止した。同州政府は収監中のイムラン・カーン元首相の政党が率いている。連邦政府はアフガニスタンと国境を接する同州の政府がイスラム過激派への対処を怠っていると主張した。

非常事態宣言と新たな知事による統治の導入で、カーン氏の野党パキスタン正義運動（ＰＴＩ）と政府との対立は急激に深まった。ＰＴＩ支持者がカーン氏の釈放を求めて首都イスラマバードへの行進を目指し、同州に集まってから１週間後の措置となった。

パキスタン憲法は、非常事態下で連邦政府が州当局に代わって統治することを認めている。タラル法相は、ここ数カ月、武装勢力による攻撃が増加しているカイバル・パクトゥンクワ州で、知事が統治を担うと述べた。

タラル氏はイスラマバードでの記者会見で、知事による統治期間は当初６カ月とするが、必要な限り継続できると説明した。内務省は同州に軍を派遣すると発表した。

連邦政府と軍は、ＰＴＩが武装勢力を抑え込めていないと非難している。ＰＴＩはこれを否定し、連邦政府が必要な資金や装備を提供していないと主張している。

カーン氏の側近でＰＴＩ報道官のズルフィカル・ブハリ氏は、政府の措置について「非常事態を装ったクーデターだ」と述べた。さらなる流血や不安定化を招く恐れがあり、抗議行動の阻止が狙いだと指摘した。

item.title: Indian central bank curbs to temper corporate rush to hedge against rupee weakness
item.description: The Indian central bank's latest measures to support the plunging rupee will raise the cost of buying protection against further weakness and slow a hedging surge that had become an additional drag on the currency, six bankers said.
item.dc:creator: Nimesh Vora, Jaspreet Kalra
item.content:encoded: The Indian central bank's [USN:L1N45W00Y TEXT:"latest measures"] to support the plunging rupee will raise the cost of buying protection against further weakness and slow a hedging surge that had become an additional drag on the currency, six bankers said. The Indian rupee, the region's worst-performing currency, has lost nearly 7% so far this year and faced persistent pressure from surging oil prices and heavy foreign outflows from local equities. The rupee fell near its all-time low of 96.96 against the dollar last week, despite $140 billion raised via special dollar deposit schemes and higher interest rates, underscoring the challenge the [USN:L4N45T0T7 TEXT:"Reserve Bank of India"] faces in stabilizing the currency. The central bank is now trying to temper corporate hedging demand by asking banks to maintain reserves against large hedges while limiting the common practice of rebooking cancelled rupee-linked derivative contracts. The measures could increase hedging costs by 80-150 basis points, depending on how much of the additional cost banks pass on to clients, the bankers said, requesting anonymity because they are not authorized to speak to the media. The reserve requirement will apply to derivative transactions used to buy foreign currency against the rupee to hedge current account payments above $2 million each. It will not apply to capital-account transactions, such as hedging foreign equity or debt investments and repaying principal amounts from overseas borrowings, one of the bankers explained. Banks typically charge importers a fixed margin in paisa terms for such transactions, which is relatively small for medium- and large-sized clients and somewhat higher for smaller ones, a second banker said. That he said is no longer feasible. Corporate purchases of forward dollars rose to a record $77 billion in September, up 80% from a year earlier, while corresponding sales were relatively subdued at $41 billion, clearing house data showed. Bankers said the measures aim to curb speculative activity by making it harder for companies to repeatedly cancel and rebook positions, while increasing compliance requirements for hedging transactions. 'MIDNIGHT OIL' The RBI's curbs caught market participants off guard and prompted a flurry of calls and meetings between treasury officials and corporate clients over the weekend, three of the bankers cited above said. "Bankers burnt midnight oil after the measures, similar to how the RBI did it appears," a foreign exchange salesperson at a large global lender said, whose team rushed to set up procedures, answer client queries and vet regulatory language to have systems in place for Monday morning trading. The steps sparked a rally in the rupee in New York trading hours, which is expected to extend after onshore markets open on Monday at 9 a.m. IST. Bankers' dollar-rupee forward premiums are set to fall as the rupee surges. Beyond tightening curbs on corporate dollar demand, the RBI has sought to temper pressure on the rupee by allowing oil marketing companies to buy dollars directly from the central bank through a special window. "The RBI is directly targeting two major sources of daily dollar demand: oil companies and importers," said Kunal Kurani, vice president at Mecklai Financial. "However, past experience suggests that these kinds of fixes have limited staying power unless the underlying pressures on the currency begin to abate."

item.title: 北朝鮮が複数の弾道ミサイル、異なる種類と韓国軍 1発は900キロ以上飛行
item.description: [ソウル／東京 １２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ソウル／東京 １２日 ロイター] - 日韓の防衛当局は１２日、北朝鮮が東岸沖へ複数の弾道ミサイルを発射したと発表した。北朝鮮によるミサイル発射はこの１カ月で４回目。一方、韓国は先週、極超音速ミサイルの発射実験を実施していた。

韓国軍合同参謀本部によると、北朝鮮は午前９時２０分ごろ、平壌付近から複数のミサイルを発射した。異なる種類のミサイルとみられ、このうち１種類は９００キロ以上飛行した。

日本の防衛省は、北朝鮮が少なくとも２発を発射したと発表。午前９時１９分ごろの１発目は最高高度２０キロ程度、飛行距離約２２０キロ、２発目は最高高度約７０キロ、飛行距離約９１０キロと分析している。日本の排他的経済水域（ＥＥＺ）への飛来は確認していないという。２発目は変則軌道で飛行した可能性があるとし、日米韓で連携して分析している。

韓国大統領府の国家安保室は緊急会議を開き、発射は国連安全保障理事会決議に違反すると非難。直ちに中止するよう北朝鮮に求めた。

韓国と北朝鮮双方が兵器の発射実験を行う中、朝鮮半島ではここ数週間、緊張が高まっている。韓国の李在明大統領は先週、国産の極超音速ミサイルの初の発射実験を視察した。韓国大統領がミサイル実験を公に視察するのは異例。

韓国軍合同参謀本部の報道官は、今回の北朝鮮による発射について「わが国の極超音速ミサイルの発射実験成功に対抗した武力誇示であると同時に、ミサイル能力を意図的に誇示する狙いがあるとみられる」との見方を示した。

北朝鮮は今月３日にも弾道ミサイルを発射。国営の朝鮮中央通信（ＫＣＮＡ）は、金正恩朝鮮労働党総書記の指導の下で実施された極超音速ミサイルの発射実験だったと報じた。

先月には南北軍事境界線付近で地雷が爆発し、韓国兵３人が負傷した。韓国側は北朝鮮が地雷を埋設したとして謝罪を要求したが、北朝鮮は否定し、韓国側による挑発だと反発している。

北朝鮮は今年、１０回を超えるミサイル発射実験を実施している。韓国国防省の元職員で大田大学の宋成宗教授は、異例の頻度で発射実験を繰り返しているのは、金総書記とトランプ米大統領による首脳会談の可能性を見据え、交渉力を高める狙いがあると指摘。「トランプ氏と会談する前に、自らの立場の価値を高める必要があるのは間違いない」と述べた。

item.title: テニス＝マスターズ上海大会、坂本は3回戦敗退 ズベレフら勝利
item.description: ［１１日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１１日　ロイター］ - 男子テニスのマスターズ上海大会は１１日、中国の上海でシングルス３回戦を行い、予選から勝ち上がった坂本怜は第９シードのアレックス・デミノー（オーストラリア）に６─７、４─６のストレートで敗れ、１６強入りを逃した。

第１シードのアレクサンダー・ズベレフ（ドイツ）はカンタン・アリス（フランス）を６─４、６─７、６─３で下し、４回戦に進出した。

一方、第３シードのベン・シェルトン（米国）は世界ランキング５６位のアルトゥール・ジェア（フランス）に６─７、６─７で敗れる波乱があった。世界４位のシェルトンは両セットともタイブレークで落とし、ジェアはトップ１０選手から初勝利を挙げた。

第７シードのフランシス・ティアフォー（米国）も第２５シードのアレハンドロ・ダビドビッチ・フォキナ（スペイン）に６─７、６─４、６─７で敗れた。

item.title: Ｆ１＝フェルスタッペンが2連勝、シンガポールＧＰ初制覇
item.description: ［シンガポール １１日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［シンガポール　１１日　ロイター］ - 自動車レースＦ１の第１７戦、シンガポール・グランプリ（ＧＰ）は１１日、シンガポールで決勝を行い、レッドブルのマックス・フェルスタッペン（オランダ）がポールトゥウィンを決めて今季２勝目を挙げた。

レース開始直後から主導権を握ったフェルスタッペンは、シャルル・ルクレール（モナコ、フェラーリ）からの序盤の攻勢を凌ぎ、シンガポールＧＰ初優勝を飾った。

同スプリントも制していたフェルスタッペンは、先週末のバーレーンＧＰから２連勝。レース後には「時間がかかったが、非常に良いレースができた。ソフトタイヤでは必要な場面で十分なスピードを発揮できた。ミディアムタイヤではみんな苦労していたようだが、それでもうまくいった。ここで勝ててとても嬉しい。ここ２戦はわれわれにとって本当にポジティブな結果が続いていて素晴らしい」と述べた。

２位はルクレールで、３位にはドライバーズランキング首位のキミ・アントネッリ（イタリア、メルセデス）が入った。同ランキングでチームメートのジョージ・ラッセル（英国）に１０２ポイント差をつけたアントネッリは、早ければ次戦の米国ＧＰでタイトルを確定させる可能性がある。

item.title: Shares supported as oil retreats; focus turns to US CPI, earnings
item.description: European shares and US futures edged higher on Monday after a choppy session in Asia as oil prices retreated, while investors looked ahead to key US inflation data and the beginning of the earnings season.
item.dc:creator: Danilo Masoni, Wayne Cole
item.content:encoded: European shares and US futures edged higher on Monday after a [USN:L1N45Y01L TEXT:"choppy session"] in Asia as [USN:L1N45Y04O TEXT:"oil prices retreated"], while investors looked ahead to key US inflation data and the beginning of the earnings season. Oil prices eased despite strikes on [USN:L1N45X06W TEXT:"shipping"] and [USN:L1N45X01E TEXT:"airports"] in the Gulf after [USN:L1N45X021 TEXT:"US President Donald Trump"] unveiled an energy-related ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia and [USN:L1N45X03S TEXT:"proposed"] that Moscow increase diesel exports. Details, however, remained unclear and the plan faced political opposition in Washington. Brent started higher in Asia before turning lower and was recently down 0.3% at $104.37 a barrel, below a recent top of $109.97, while US crude futures lost 0.6% to $91.33. Deutsche Bank strategist Jim Reid said the outlook for oil remained uncertain. "So even if a Russia/Ukraine ceasefire and Russian diesel waiver ease pressure on refined products, attacks on Riyadh and fighting around Bab el-Mandeb leave an upside tail risk for oil and shipping costs, alongside continuing Strait of Hormuz disruption," he said. Lower crude prices helped support sentiment in Europe, where the region-wide STOXX 600 (.STOXX) rose 0.6% at 0742 GMT, aided by gains from automakers (.SXAP) after [USN:L1N45Y047 TEXT:"China and the European Union reached agreements"] on hybrid vehicle exports. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares excluding Japan (.MISX00000PUS) was down 0.5% and Chinese blue chips (.CSI300) dipped 0.7%. South Korean stocks (.KS11) fell 3.6% and Taiwanese shares (.TWII) were unchanged. On Wall Street, S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures rose around 0.3%. Activity was subdued with Japan closed for a holiday and the US Treasury market shut for Columbus Day, leaving trading thin ahead of earnings season, with major US banks including JPMorgan (JPM.N) and Goldman Sachs (GS.N) reporting on Tuesday, followed by Bank of America (BAC.N) on Wednesday. [USN:L4N45T028 TEXT:"TSMC 2330.TW"], the world's largest manufacturer of advanced AI chips, will likely report a sixth consecutive quarter of record earnings on Thursday. Earnings from chip-equipment maker ASML (ASML.AS) are due on Wednesday. S&P 500 earnings are expected to jump more than 30% in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES, though the bulk of that comes from the tech sector. STOXX earnings are expected to increase 21%, or 9.7% excluding the energy sector. Treasury yields hit 24-year highs this month as elevated energy costs fuelled concerns that inflation could stay elevated, keeping policymakers hawkish and pressuring equity valuations. On Monday, euro area benchmark [USN:L6N45Y09K TEXT:"Bund yields edged lower"] and French and Italian debt risk premiums fell slightly. US CPI TO HEAT UP, BUT CORE COOLER The market faces fresh challenges this week from US data on consumer and producer prices and retail sales. Rising energy costs are expected to lift CPI by a hefty 0.6% to an annual 3.7%, though the core is seen cooler at 0.2% and 2.5%. "Oil prices remain higher than we had assumed as shipping costs have soared and product prices are even higher," said Bruce Kasman, head of global economics at JPMorgan. "The signals on inflation point to a sharp rebound in headline inflation that will squeeze purchasing power and a firming in core inflation that will keep central banks focused on near-term hikes." Markets imply only an 18% chance of a rate rise from the Federal Reserve this month, rising to an 85% chance of a hike in December. Investors are also wagering on hikes in the EU, Japan and Britain before the end of the year. In currency markets, the euro remained on the defensive at $1.1205 , having fallen for five weeks straight amid concerns about government deficits in Europe. The dollar index held near 17-month highs at 102.21 , but it has stalled against the yen at 158.44 , as the threat of Japanese intervention deters speculators for now. In commodity markets, non-interest-bearing gold rose 0.1% to $4,198 an ounce , having managed to bounce more than 1% last week.

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝ＦＡ見込みのカブス鈴木「自分にとって初めての経験」
item.description: ［１１日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１１日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）カブスの鈴木誠也外野手（３２）が、今季終了後にフリーエージェント（ＦＡ）となる見通しを受け、チームで過ごした５年間を振り返った。ＭＬＢ公式サイトが伝えた。

カブスは今季のプレーオフで敗退。鈴木は同球団での最終戦となった可能性について聞かれると、「いい思い出を全て話そうとしたら、３時間くらいかかる。それでもいいか」と冗談交じりに語った。

また、渡米後初めて所属したチームがカブスだったことに触れ、チームメートやスタッフ、熱狂的なファンへの感謝の気持ちを伝え、「家族もシカゴが大好き。ただ、ＦＡは自分にとって初めての経験。いろいろなプロセスがあると思うので、どうなるか分からない」と述べた。

鈴木は２０２２年３月、プロ野球広島から５年総額８５００万ドル（約１３４億円）で加入。５年間で通算６７５試合に出場し、打率２割６分９厘、１１３本塁打、３８２打点を記録した。今季は打率２割７分、２６本塁打、８６打点で、自己最多の８１四球を選んだ。

自身の５年間については「周囲や自分自身の期待に応えられたか分からない。毎年、シーズンが終わるたびに悔しさがあったように思う」と厳しく評価する一方、「自分は成長できたと思うし、一生懸命努力してきた」と語り、今季は守備面で大きく成長できたと手応えを示した。

SYDNEY: Stock markets got off to an erratic start on Monday (Oct 12) as earnings season loomed, while oil slipped amid confusion over whether Russia would, or could, increase energy exports. While the conflict in the Gulf continued with strikes on shipping and airports, President Donald Trump's announcement of an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia muddied the waters on oil supply. Trump's proposal for Russia to increase its exports of diesel added to the mix, though it also drew opposition from Republican and Democratic senators as potentially illegal. Brent futures started higher but soon slipped 1.6 per cent to US$103.01 a barrel, below a recent top of US$109.97, while US crude futures lost 1.9 per cent to US$90.11 a barrel.

South Korean stocks fell 2.2 per cent and Taiwanese shares eased 0.5 per cent. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares excluding Japan dipped 0.3 per cent, while Chinese blue chips added 0.1 per cent. On Wall Street, S&P 500 futures edged up 0.3 per cent, while Nasdaq futures firmed 0.4 per cent. In Europe, EUROSTOXX 50 futures firmed 0.5 per cent, DAX futures gained 0.6 per cent and FTSE futures added 0.4 per cent. Trade was thin with Japanese markets shut and the US on a partial holiday ahead of earnings season, with major US banks kicking off on Tuesday. TSMC, the world's largest manufacturer of advanced AI chips, will likely report a sixth consecutive quarter of record earnings on Thursday. S&P 500 earnings are expected to jump by more than 30 per cent in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES, though the bulk of that comes from the tech sector. My Bui, an economist at AMP, said all the gains in the S&P 500 since mid-September had been in tech, while investors were demanding higher yields to fund the massive borrowing for AI. The US investment-grade credit default swap index, which tracks the cost of insurance against default, had also risen sharply to its highest level since the US-Israeli war on Iran began. "Overall, wider spreads suggest investors are questioning whether AI revenues can keep pace with rising borrowing costs," Bui said. "Corporate bond issuance to fund AI capex, combined with wider high-yield spreads, will raise refinancing costs as the current wave of debt matures over the next few years." US CPI TO HEAT UP, BUT CORE COOLER The flood of corporate debt has added to pressure in sovereign markets, driving Treasury yields to 24-year highs last week while lifting the discount applied to company earnings. The market faces fresh challenges this week from US data on consumer and producer prices and retail sales. Rising energy costs are expected to lift CPI by a hefty 0.6 per cent to an annual 3.7 per cent, though the core is seen cooler at 0.2 per cent and 2.5 per cent. "Oil prices remain higher than we had assumed as shipping costs have soared and product prices are even higher," said Bruce Kasman, head of global economics at JPMorgan. "The signals on inflation point to a sharp rebound in headline inflation that will squeeze purchasing power and a firming in core inflation that will keep central banks focused on near-term hikes." Markets imply only an 18 per cent chance of a rate rise from the Federal Reserve this month, rising to an 85 per cent chance of a hike in December. Investors are also wagering on hikes in the EU, Japan and Britain before the end of the year. In currency markets, the euro remained on the defensive at US$1.1201, having fallen for five weeks straight amid concerns about government deficits in Europe. The dollar index held near 17-month highs at 102.25, but it has stalled on the yen at 158.19 as the threat of Japanese intervention deters speculators for now. In commodity markets, non-interest-bearing gold rose 0.4 per cent to US$4,212 an ounce, having managed to bounce more than 1 per cent last week.

Source: Reuters/ec

item.title: ゴルフ＝米沢が日本勢最高9位、松山21位 ベイカレント・クラシック
item.description: ［１１日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１１日　ロイター］ - 米男子ゴルフの秋季シリーズ、ベイカレント・クラシック・レクサスは１１日、神奈川県横浜ＣＣ（パー７１）で最終ラウンドを行い、前日２９位の米沢蓮が１イーグル、６バーディー、１ボギーの７アンダー６４をマークし、通算１２アンダーの２７２で日本勢最高の９位に入った。

米沢は１番でバーディーを奪うと、３番から３連続バーディーを記録。６番ではイーグルを決め、９番でもバーディーを奪うなど、この日出場選手のベストスコアをたたき出した。

２９位スタートの松山英樹は６バーディー、２ボギーの６７で回り、通算９アンダーの２７５で２１位。金谷拓実と砂川公佑が２３位、石坂友宏が２９位、細野勇策と藤本佳則が３３位、久常涼と香妻陣一朗が４１位、中島啓太が５０位、岩崎亜久竜が５４位、岩田寛が６７位、アマチュアの長崎煌心が６９位だった。

前日首位のマイケル・ブレナン（米国）が４バーディー、１ボギーの６８で回り、通算１６アンダーの２６８で優勝。今季２勝目、ツアー通算３勝目を挙げた。

item.title: One dead in new attack on Saudi airport, a day after Houthi strike kills 13
item.description: Saudi-led coalition forces in Yemen said an unidentified projectile had targeted Riyadh's international airport Terminal 4 on Sunday, causing a fire. Eleven people were wounded in addition to the fatality, the Saudi civil aviation authority said.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

One dead in new attack on Saudi airport, a day after Houthi strike kills 13

Saudi-led coalition forces in Yemen said an unidentified projectile had targeted Riyadh's international airport Terminal 4 on Sunday, causing a fire. Eleven people were wounded in addition to the fatality, the Saudi civil aviation authority said.

An air traffic control tower is seen at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Sep 19, 2026. (File photo: AFP)

FAST

RIYADH: One person was killed and nearly a dozen hurt in a new attack on Riyadh's international airport on Sunday (Oct 11), Saudi authorities reported, a day after a strike claimed by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300. Saudi-led coalition forces in Yemen said an unidentified projectile had targeted Riyadh's international airport Terminal 4 on Sunday, causing a fire. Eleven people were wounded in addition to the fatality, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. Coalition forces also said Saudi air defences had intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of King Khalid International Airport. They later added that a drone had been intercepted and destroyed in the country's Eastern Province, and a ballistic missile launched towards Khamis Mushait had been intercepted.  Emergency alerts were also issued in Abha, in the south, early on Monday but the danger had since passed, the Saudi Civil Defense said.

The strikes have exposed vulnerabilities in Saudi defence capabilities as the kingdom wages an air campaign against the Houthis, who are fighting a ground war in Yemen against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government. Footage released by Saudi state television of the Saturday attack on the Riyadh airport showed scores of religious pilgrims lined up at a gate as they prepared to travel to Islam's two holiest sites. A bright orange flash sent people running in panic, while parts of the roof appeared to cave in. The airport was closed after the attack, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade. HOUTHIS CLAIM RESPONSIBILITY FOR OTHER ATTACKS In a televised speech on Sunday, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed responsibility for Saturday's attack and said the group had struck the airport in Dammam in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province and two facilities of Saudi oil giant Saudi Aramco. The Saudi government's media office and Aramco did not respond to requests for comment. The Saudi civil aviation authority confirmed the strike on Dammam's King Fahd International Airport late on Sunday, adding that "damage assessments and safety inspections of airport facilities are under way."

Related:

Saudi Arabia says three killed at airport as Yemen war expands

Singapore condemns Houthi attacks on civilian aviation infrastructure in Saudi Arabia

An eyewitness aboard a taxiing aircraft at Dammam told Reuters that around 8.30pm (1.30am, Monday, Singapore time) on Sunday, they saw a projectile strike the tarmac beside several parked aircraft, causing a fire. The witness said the aircraft returned to the gate. Passengers disembarked and were told to leave. Flight-tracking website Flightradar24 showed several delays and cancellations on Sunday for arrivals and departures at Dammam airport, the kingdom's third-largest. The Houthis earlier on Sunday had renewed their warning against using Saudi airports. "We urge everyone to take our warnings seriously, and Saudi Arabia bears responsibility for any failed interceptions," the group said. Britain's embassy in Saudi Arabia in a post on X advised British citizens against all but essential travel to Jeddah, Dammam and all airports in the kingdom except the airport in Medina. US aviation authorities issued a notice to US airlines to use caution while flying to or over the kingdom.

"WORSE IS YET TO COME," HOUTHIS WARN Saudi Arabia has recently stepped up its military involvement in Yemen, launching strikes against the Houthis and backing a government counteroffensive after the Houthis seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month. The Houthis said on Sunday that Saudi Arabia carried out 124 air strikes in Yemen in the past 24 hours. "Unless the Saudi enemy stops its aggression and interference in Yemen, worse is yet to come, God willing," Yemen's Houthi-run foreign ministry said in statements carried by Al Masirah television. US President Donald Trump said on Saturday the United States was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the wider war with Iran that the US and Israel launched in February. In a post on Telegram, Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araqchi said he told his Saudi counterpart that Tehran was ready to help facilitate dialogue between Saudi Arabia and Yemen.

Related:

Türkiye sending technical, defensive support to Saudi Arabia to help fight Houthis, officials say

ENERGY CONFERENCE STILL GOING AHEAD A five-day conference of international energy organisation WPC Energy opened as planned on Sunday at a convention centre about 10km from the Riyadh airport, the Saudi energy ministry said. A ministerial meeting of the International Energy Forum also went ahead, according to a media advisory from the ministry. It was not clear which ministers attended. Italy's energy minister, Gilberto Pichetto Fratin, whose country was co-hosting, had said on Friday he would participate remotely via video link. German officials were trying to organise a return flight for economy minister Katherina Reiche. She was supposed to return to Berlin from Riyadh on Monday but the ministry said it appeared likely her flight would be unable to take off. Separately, Saudi authorities announced that in-person classes at schools in Riyadh would be shifted to remote learning from Sunday until Thursday. Sunday's attack brought the death toll in attacks on Riyadh's airport to 18 for the week. In Saturday's attack, the dead included four Saudis while the remainder were foreign nationals, Saudi authorities said.

Source: Reuters/rk

item.title: 米アマゾン、ＡＩ新興デカートの買収協議 70億ドル規模＝ＷＳＪ
item.description: [１１日 ロイター] - 米アマゾン・ドット・コムが人工知能（ＡＩ）新興企業デカートの買収に向けて協議しており、買収額...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米アマゾン、ＡＩ新興デカートの買収協議　70億ドル規模＝ＷＳＪ 9:25 配信

写真はデカートのロゴ。2026年8月16日撮影。 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

[１１日 ロイター] - 米アマゾン・ドット・コムが人工知能（ＡＩ）新興企業デカートの買収に向けて協議しており、買収額は約７０億ドルに達する可能性があると、米紙ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナル（ＷＳＪ）が１１日、関係者の話として報じた。

• デカートのウェブサイトによると、同社のモデル「ルーシー」はライブ映像をリアルタイムで編集できる。ロボットや自動運転システムの訓練・試験に使うシミュレーション環境を生成するモデル「オアシス」も開発している。

• ＷＳＪがピッチブックのデータを基に報じたところによると、デカートの５月時点の評価額は４０億ドル近くだった。同社には米半導体大手エヌビディアが出資している。

• ロイターは現時点で報道を確認できていない。デカートとアマゾンのコメントは得られていない。

• 報道によると、交渉が決裂したり、別の買い手候補が現れたりしなければ、近く合意に至る可能性がある。

• ブルームバーグによると、アンソロピックは９月、デューデリジェンス（資産査定）を実施した後、デカートの買収を見送ることを決めた。同社は８月、６０億ドル規模となる可能性のある取引を検討していたという。

• デカートは５月、ラディカル・ベンチャーズ主導の資金調達ラウンドで３億ドルを調達し、エヌビディアが新規投資家として参加した。

item.title: パレスチナ議会選延期、来年9月に議長選と同時実施へ
item.description:
Ali Sawafta Nidal al-Mughrabi Eman Abouhassira
[ラマラ １０日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Ali Sawafta　Nidal al-Mughrabi　Eman Abouhassira

[ラマラ １０日 ロイター] - パレスチナ自治政府のアッバス議長は１０日、１１月に予定していた評議会（議会）選挙を来年９月１１日に延期し、同日に自治政府議長選も実施すると発表した。延期の理由として、イスラエルの措置とパレスチナ自治区の治安情勢を挙げた。

パレスチナ自治政府の公式通信社ＷＡＦＡによると、アッバス氏の議長令は「イスラエルの措置による障害」に言及し、政治面や治安面を含め、現地で「自由で公正かつ包摂的な選挙」に適した条件を整える必要があるとした。

これに対しイスラエルのサール外相はＸへの投稿で、パレスチナで最後に選挙が行われたのは２０年前だと指摘。アッバス氏の説明について「責任と説明責任を逃れるための、またしてもばかげたうそだ」と一蹴した。

自治政府の選挙が１１月に実施されるかどうかは、以前から強く疑問視されていた。パレスチナでは２００５─０６年を最後に、議会選も議長選も行われていない。その後、アッバス氏と対立するイスラム組織ハマスが同氏側の勢力を排除し、ガザ地区の支配権を握った。

アッバス氏は０９年に議長としての任期が切れて以降、議長令による統治を続けている。

議長令は、東エルサレムを含むヨルダン川西岸でのイスラエル軍の攻撃、入植地の拡大、入植者による暴力、移動制限に加え、イスラエルがパレスチナ側の税収を差し止め続けていることが、１１月の選挙の準備と実施を困難にしているとした。

ガザについては「極めて厳しい治安・人道状況」を挙げ、イスラエル軍の撤退が完了していないこと、復興が進んでいないこと、国際安定化部隊と警察の展開に向けた取り決めが履行されていないことを指摘した。

item.title: ゴルフ＝山下がアラムコ韓国選手権で優勝、欧州ツアー2勝目
item.description: ［１１日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１１日　ロイター］ - 女子ゴルフの欧州ツアー、アラムコ韓国選手権は１１日、韓国のニューコリアＣＣ（パー７２）で最終ラウンドを行い、山下美夢有が欧州ツアー通算２勝目を挙げた。

前日首位の山下は１イーグル、７バーディー、ノーボギーのコース記録６３をマーク。通算２２アンダーの２６６で、２位に３打差をつけて優勝した。

世界ランキング５位の山下は欧州ツアー公式サイトで「とてもうれしい。今日はショットもパットも全てが非常に良かった。自分のプレーを信じていた。この大会に出場するのは初めてで、優勝できてとてもうれしい。こんなに何度も優勝できるとは思っていなかったので、そのこともうれしい」と喜びを語った。

item.title: サッカー＝鎌田がプレミア初ゴール、クリスタルパレス勝利
item.description: ［リバプール（英国） １１日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［リバプール（英国）　１１日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイングランド・プレミアリーグは１１日、各地で試合を行い、クリスタルパレスの鎌田大地がホームのノッティンガム・フォレスト戦でプレミアリーグ初ゴールを決めた。

先発した鎌田はチームが１点ビハインドで迎えた前半４１分、ゴール前至近距離で受けたパスから同点弾を記録。前半に勝ち越したクリスタルパレスは後半にも１得点を加え、３─１で勝利した。鎌田は後半４５分までプレー。チームメートの冨安健洋はメンバー外だった。

マンチェスター・シティー（マンＣ）は敵地でリバプールに３─０で勝利した。財務規定違反認定後初の試合となったマンＣは、後半１７分にリバプールのＭＦライアン・フラーフェンベルフが退場した後に主導権を握ると、同２０分にアーリング・ハーランドが先制点を記録。その後にジェレミー・ドクとラヤン・シェルキが加点し、開幕６連勝で首位をキープした。リバプールの遠藤航はベンチスタートから出番がなかった。

ハルの守田英正はホームのエバートン戦で後半３０分から途中出場。ハルは２─２で引き分けた。

item.title: サッカー＝後藤がブンデス初ゴール、鈴木は退場 フライブルク白星
item.description: ［ベルリン １１日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ベルリン　１１日　ロイター］ - サッカーのドイツ１部ブンデスリーガは１１日、各地で試合を行い、後藤啓介と鈴木唯人が所属するフライブルクはホームでシャルケに２─１で勝利した。後藤はブンデスリーガ初ゴールとなる決勝点を挙げた。

フライブルクは前半１０分に先制したが、同３０分に追いつかれた。さらに後半１９分には、先発出場した鈴木が２枚目のイエローカードを受けて退場し、数的不利に陥った。

それでも後半２４分から途中出場した後藤が同４０分、左からのクロスに頭で合わせ、勝ち越しゴールを奪った。フライブルクは開幕５試合で勝ち点を１３に伸ばし、得失点差でドルトムントを上回って首位に浮上した。

シャルケの田中聡は先発し、後半２４分までプレーした。

ボルシアＭＧは敵地でケルンに１─２で敗れ、開幕５連敗となった。橋岡大樹が先発して後半３５分までプレー。町野修斗は後半２０分、宇野禅斗は同２３分から途中出場した。

(Corrects to drop byline with no text changes) By Courtney Rozen WASHINGTON, Oct 11 : American AI developers can give the British government early access to AI models for safety testing without running afoul of US President Donald Trump's administration, the Telegraph newspaper said on Sunday. The Trump administration has reversed a decision that requested developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic not to share new AI models with Britain's AI Security Institute before release, the newspaper said.

The change signals a softer stance by the Trump administration on international AI safety efforts, giving US developers greater latitude to cooperate with Britain as policymakers grapple with how to oversee the increasingly powerful technology. Spokespersons for Trump, OpenAI and Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Reuters. Britain's AI Security Institute, set up after the world's first AI safety summit in 2023, tests the most advanced AI models to evaluate their capabilities and the risk of misuse.  Trump has repeatedly dismissed calls for binding safety requirements on AI developers, a position that appears to be shifting. His newly launched AI task force said on Friday developers must report security incidents with their AI models.

Source: Reuters
